MAJOR: `redact_reason` is heuristic regex over untrusted free-text; any token format it doesn't know (sk-, xoxb-, JWT, generic high-entropy secrets) is persisted verbatim as `rereview_reason` into repo-committed evidence JSON — redaction-as-security-boundary is not durable.

The gate only evaluates `g2.transitions(base)` (completions), so the `warn_after=2` signal never fires for items over budget that aren't completing in this diff; spec wording scopes warn unconditionally and fail to completions.

`churn_verdict` spawns `git ls-tree` over the entire review dir plus one `git show` per evidence file, per item, inside a `fast`-tier gate — O(items × review-files) subprocesses grows linearly with backlog history.

`_after_epoch` swallows all parse errors and returns `True`, so a naive/aware or differently-formatted ledger `at` silently counts every review and can spuriously fail a completion instead of surfacing a data-quality error.
MINOR: `review_budget()` raises an uncaught `ValueError` from `architect_review` run-mode (traceback exit) rather than a clean diagnostic; `review_churn_check` turns the same config error into a generic per-row exit 2.
`review_guard`'s success return (the redacted reason) is discarded and `main` re-redacts the raw reason — dead return value and duplicated redaction path.
`_ingest` archives prior evidence to `<stem>-prev-<epoch_ms>.json` via `rename`; a same-millisecond collision silently overwrites (loses) a prior review, and the name is non-deterministic.
`evaluate()`'s synthetic error rows emit `warn_after: 0`/`fail_after: 0` in `--json`, feeding machine consumers fabricated budget values.
Threshold defaults (`2`/`4`) are duplicated in code defaults, config, and docs — a config change leaves code defaults and docs stale (acceptance explicitly asks for no duplicated thresholds).
Tests never exercise the committed (`ls-tree`/`show`) path nor assert `rereview_reason` is actually persisted redacted+truncated in the evidence file.
`review_epoch` takes the last `gate==1` entry in list order, not the chronologically latest, and `latest_sha` uses lexicographic max on `at` (mixed `Z`/`+00:00` forms pick the wrong "latest").
NIT: `config/architect-review.json` includes unrelated reformatting of `blocking_findings`/`skip_globs`, inflating review noise.
Docs hardcode `warn_after (2)` / `fail_after (4)` alongside config; consider pointing at the config key only.
`review_guard`'s sha-citation requirement for `--reason` goes beyond the stated acceptance (non-empty only) — correct, but should be called out as an intentional tightening in the item record.
SUMMARY: Solid single-owner design: thresholds/counting are genuinely centralized in `architect_review.py` and both consumers reuse `churn_verdict`/`review_budget`, with fail-closed git/evidence handling and good boundary tests.
Top risks are security (heuristic redaction of committed free-text), narrow warn coverage (completions only), and unbounded per-item git subprocess cost in a fast-tier gate.
Recommend tightening evidence persistence (redact-or-refuse, deterministic archive naming) and adding committed-path + persistence assertions before relying on this as the freeze guard.
